checks.finding: Franklin County's zoning map does not cover this parcel. The county zones only the unincorporated parts of the townships under county zoning, so a city, village, or township with its own zoning decides here.
checks.limitation: No zoning conclusion either way. The county map leaving a lot out does not say which district applies.

checks.nextAction: Ask the zoning office for the city, village, or township that contains the lot which district applies.

checks.finding: FEMA's flood map puts this lot in Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard). No part of it is mapped in a Special Flood Hazard Area.
checks.limitation: FEMA's zone lines and the parcel lines come from different maps, so the edges may not line up exactly. Being outside the mapped floodplain does not mean the lot never floods. A flood zone is not a flood-insurance determination or a building permit.

sources.title: National Flood Hazard Layer: flood hazard zones

checks.nextAction: Check the current map for this lot on FEMA's Flood Map Service Center before closing; a lender may still order its own flood determination.

checks.finding: The National Wetlands Inventory maps no wetland on this lot. Franklin County's stream-buffer map puts no part of it in a riparian setback.
checks.limitation: "NWI shows none" is not a wetland delineation. The NWI is drawn from aerial imagery (here from 2007) and misses many small, forested, or seasonally dry wetlands; only a delineation in the field, confirmed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or Ohio EPA, says whether regulated wetlands are on the lot. The county's stream-buffer map covers its mapped setback watersheds; a city, village, or township with its own zoning may set its own stream rules.

checks.nextAction: If the lot has low, wet, or wooded ground, ask the county soil and water conservation district or a wetland consultant whether a wetland delineation is worth doing before you build.

checks.finding: This parcel touches the public right-of-way of W Dodridge St and Neil Ave in Franklin County's right-of-way layer. In the county engineer's road layer, the W Dodridge St centerline is about 9 m (28 ft) from the parcel.
checks.limitation: Touching a mapped right-of-way is not legal access. These layers do not show whether the lot has a recorded right to use the road, whether the road is built and maintained where the lot meets it, or whether a driveway would be permitted there.

checks.finding: No utility record has been checked for this lot.
checks.limitation: No conclusion either way: public water and sewer may reach the lot, or it may need a well and a septic system.

checks.finding: No search of recorded easements or restrictions is attached.
checks.limitation: Recorded easements, covenants, or restrictions can limit where and what you build. None are ruled in or out.
checks.nextAction: Ask a title company to search the recorded documents for this parcel.

checks.finding: The seller's right to sell this lot has not been verified.
checks.limitation: This report does not check ownership records or the seller's identity. Sellers who impersonate the real owner often target vacant land (see the linked ALTA guidance).
checks.nextAction: Have a title company confirm the owner of record and reach the owner through contact details it finds independently, not ones the seller supplied.

checks.finding: No survey of this lot is attached.
checks.limitation: The boundary shown comes from Ohio's statewide parcel map (OGRIP), which is not a survey. The real corners and lines can differ.
checks.nextAction: Hire a licensed Ohio surveyor to locate the boundary before you close.

checks.finding: No septic site review is on file for this lot.
checks.limitation: If public sewer does not reach the lot, a septic system needs a site and soil evaluation before anyone can say one will work.
checks.nextAction: If the lot has no sewer, ask the health district for a site and soil evaluation before you close.
